audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[].side was 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] read Skill/Galio/Galio/Galio/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora, matching packet.levelChart. Six rows disagreed across layers.
audit.why: The content verdict is the defensible one: Galio owns 2 through 4-5 because Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1, and Aurora takes over from 6 once Between Worlds gives her a leap plus a teleport zone.
audit.corrected: Moved phases[1..6].side onto the content/packet verdict with ratings and whys rewritten in the same group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and late rows were generic Galio boilerplate about MR and AP trades, and the content layer described her passive as something she 'stacks with autos' for burst.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration heals her off spirits exorcised by her spells and attacks — it is sustain, not a burst stack, and it is what makes Grievous Wounds timing matter here.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the rows and the early/wants fields around the heal and around her two hop cooldowns.
sources: enemyKit P text and heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated the interaction that decides every all-in: Justice Punch's knockup shuts off Across the Veil and Between Worlds. wants.foe[1] also claimed Between Worlds has an 'untargetable window'.
audit.why: Both of her escapes are dashes, and a knockup denies a dash. Riot's text gives Between Worlds a leap, a shockwave and a slow zone — no untargetability anywhere; the invisibility is on Across the Veil.
audit.corrected: Stated the dash denial across the chart, trades and Do's, and rewrote wants.foe[1] to the leap.
sources: enemyKit W and R dash flags

audit.why: It is the field that carries the numbers.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil 22s at rank 1, The Weirding 15s, Twofold Hex 9s, Between Worlds 140s at rank 1.
